item.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data and Source Code
item.description: Hackers breached 1Password's backend systems through a compromised employee GitHub account, stealing customer information and private source code.
item.dc:creator: Dark Web Informer
item.content:encoded:
Hackers breached 1Password's backend systems through a compromised employee GitHub account, stealing customer information and private source code.

The attackers pushed malicious code into backend services and accessed the company's CI/CD infrastructure. Stolen records included customer names, email addresses, account identifiers, sign-in timestamps, and tokens from certain invitation and account recovery links.

1Password confirmed that customer password vaults, stored secrets, and encryption keys were not compromised. The company also found no evidence of account takeovers and says customers do not need to reset their passwords.

The breach was discovered on November 19. Since then, 1Password has disabled the compromised GitHub account, rotated potentially exposed credentials, and strengthened security controls. Recovery verification codes have also been expanded from six digits to ten alphanumeric characters, while external cybersecurity experts review the company's response.

Source: https://1password.com/blog/update-on-nov-2026-security-incident
